item.title: MC Gawthi at Rolling Loud India 2026: Pune's Marathi Rapper Is Stepping Up
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: MC Gawthi, Pune's Marathi rapper, plays Rolling Loud India 2026 on Dec 13. Songs to know and ticket info inside.
item.content:encoded:
A grassroots Marathi voice, a fresh Gully Gang Records collab and a festival slot.

Rolling Loud India's 2026 lineup leans hard into the country's grassroots hip-hop circuit, and MC Gawthi, a Marathi rapper from Pune, is that circuit in person. He plays Sunday, December 13 at Rolling Loud India.

Who is MC Gawthi?

Pune-based and rooted in the Pimpri-Chinchwad area, Gawthi works in independent Marathi rap. Hip Hop Magazine, in its write-up of his single "Company", frames him as a grassroots rapper whose career rests on steady releases rather than one overnight hit. He describes the "gangster" label as a stance on loyalty, not criminality.

Songs to know

  • "Company" (2026), produced by SANDSTRM and released in January 2026
  • "Tap Kar" (May 2026), a Hindi-language single with Mumbai's MC Altaf and producer Year Down, out via Gully Gang Records and Universal Music India, per Shazam
  • "Khunnas" (2025), with producer Audiocrackerr
  • Earlier singles on Apple Music include "Numberkari" and "302" (2024), and "Most Wanted" and "Rx100" (2022)

Why catch the set

A Pune-to-Mumbai link-up with MC Altaf signals momentum, and a festival like this is exactly where grassroots names become headline conversations. If you like your rap local, direct and lyric-first, this is a set for the early crowd.

Plan your Sunday

MC Gawthi performs on day two, Sunday, December 13, of Rolling Loud India 2026 in Mumbai. Tickets are on the District app, and the venue is still to be announced. Everything you need is at rollingloud.com/india.

item.title: 9 Wine Gifts Clients Remember After the Holidays
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: Nine client wine gifts from $15.75 to $294.95 at Wine Express, with the shipping, signature, and timing rules to know before you order.
item.content:encoded:
Nine bottles at nine price points, plus the delivery rules that decide whether the gift arrives at all.

Disclosure: YourInfoDaily may earn a commission if you buy through links in this article. This content is intended for readers 21 and over.

The client gifts people remember look chosen, arrive on time, and get opened. A bottle with a story clears all three bars for less than most branded gift boxes, and the nine below cover budgets from a thank-you note to a closed deal.

All prices are as listed in the Wine Express gifting section on October 10, 2026. Most were shown as sale prices, so confirm before you order.

The nine bottles

1. Mionetto Prosecco Brut, Treviso DOC: $15.75

The volume play. With 30 names on the list, a recognizable Prosecco with a handwritten note beats a forgettable fruit basket. Listed with a 94-point score.

2. Fabio Cordella 2020 Il Castellano Primitivo, Salento: $16.47

A rich southern Italian red at a price that lets you send two. Good for the client who cooks.

3. Fabio Cordella 2018 Ronaldinho R10 Primitivo, Salento: $24.95

A bottle named after the Brazilian football legend is a conversation starter before the cork comes out. For clients in sports, music, or entertainment, that is the point.

4. Chateau Ausone 2015 Le Petit Vauthier, Saint-Emilion Grand Cru: $37.95

Bordeaux with nearly a decade of age, tied to one of Saint-Emilion's most famous estates. It reads as far more expensive than it is.

5. Nickel & Nickel 2023 Chardonnay, Truchard Vineyard, Carneros: $49.95

A single-vineyard Napa-area white from a name wine drinkers know. Safe for a client whose taste you cannot guess.

6. Moët & Chandon Brut Imperial: $52.95

The universal signal for congratulations. Send it for a launch, a funding round, or a signed contract. Listed with a 94-point score.

7. Belle Glos 2022 Pinot Noir, Clark & Telephone Vineyard, Magnum: $85.95

A magnum is a double-size bottle, and its size is a statement. This is the gift for a team, an office, or a client who hosts.

8. Laurent-Perrier Cuvée Rosé Brut Champagne, Gift Box: $92.95

Rose Champagne that arrives already boxed. Rated 95 points, it suits anniversaries of a working relationship and your most loyal accounts.

9. Louis Latour 2023 Corton-Charlemagne: $294.95

Grand Cru white Burgundy, rated 98 points. Reserve it for the 

one relationship that carried your year.

[Browse the full Wine Express gifting section.]

How to pick by relationship

  • New or small accounts: bottles 1 through 3. Keep it warm, not lavish.
  • Steady clients and referral sources: bottles 4 through 6. Recognizable names do the work.
  • Top accounts, partners, investors: bottles 7 through 9. Scale or rarity says what a card cannot.

If you want something between a bottle and a full case, the same section listed a WSET Level I in Wines Tasting Sampler at $149.99, a structured tasting set for the client who wants to learn.

The delivery rules that make or break a wine gift

Wine is not like sending a candle. Read these before you load a spreadsheet of addresses.

  • An adult must sign. Every delivery requires a signature and ID from someone 21 or older. Wine Express recommends a work address for client gifts.
  • Missed deliveries cost you. If the carrier cannot get a signature and the box is returned, the sender pays return shipping plus a 20% restocking fee.
  • Some states are off the list. Wine Express does not ship to Alabama, Alaska, Arkansas, Delaware, Hawaii, Kentucky, Michigan, Mississippi, North Dakota, South Dakota, Tennessee, Utah, or Puerto Rico.
  • Champagne takes longer. Champagne orders need three to five days of processing and cannot be expedited.
  • Order early. In-stock wines typically arrive 2 to 14 business days after ordering, depending on location, and shipments can be delayed in extreme weather.

For a mid-December arrival, order before Thanksgiving week.

What a recipient sees

Wine Express leaves pricing out of gift packages, so the client sees the bottle and not the receipt. The company doesn't sell gift certificates, so every gift ships physically.

How to make shipping free

Ground shipping is free on orders of $149 or more, or 12 or more bottles, going to the same address. That helps when you are sending a case to one office. Gifts going to many different addresses are charged per shipment, as shown at checkout, so add that to your per-client budget.

One workaround: ship a case to yourself for free, then hand-deliver to local clients. A bottle handed over in person is remembered longer anyway.

A note on etiquette

Check a client's gift policy before sending anything over a modest amount. Some companies and most public agencies cap or ban gifts. And if you do not know whether someone drinks, ask a colleague or choose a different gift.

[Start your client list at Wine Express while holiday delivery windows are open.]

FAQ

How much should I spend on a client wine gift?

Match the relationship. The bottles range from $15.75 to $294.95, and most client gifts fall in the $25 to $95 range.

Can I include a note?

Add your gift message at checkout and confirm the options there. For wine club gifts, Wine Express says a handwritten card can be added by calling customer care.

Can I send wine to a client's home?

Yes, if the state is served and an adult 21 or older can sign. A work address is usually the safer choice.

Will the price show on the package?

No. Wine Express says pricing is not included in gift orders.

item.title: Vichaar: The Dehradun Rapper and Designer Hitting Rolling Loud India
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: Vichaar, the Dehradun rapper from MTV Hustle 4 and the Alter Ego EP, joins Rolling Loud India 2026 in Mumbai. Here's who he is.
item.content:encoded:
From NIFT Gandhinagar to MTV Hustle 4, Vichaar swapped a creative-director job for the mic.

Most rappers don't start out with a design portfolio. Vichaar did. The Dehradun-raised artist and former art director is on the bill for Rolling Loud India, where he hits the stage on Saturday, December 12, 2026, in Mumbai.

From design desks to the booth

According to StarsUnfolded, Vichaar's real name is Abhin Pandita, and he is from Dehradun. He studied at NIFT Gandhinagar and, before committing to music, worked in design and creative roles, including as creative director at Img Creators, which he left in 2023 to focus on rap. Early tracks "Azaad" and "Asar Hai Kya" went up on YouTube while he was still a student.

What to know

His first EP, Alter Ego, arrived in July 2024, and he competed on MTV Hustle 4 that year. His JioSaavn catalog includes "Mudda Kya Hai," "Kalakaari Vishwasniya," and "5 Fingers of Death," with a Red Bull 64 Bars cut, "UNDERDOG SHIT," listed as his latest release (September 2026).

He also appears on "United by Hip Hop" (2025), a multilingual posse cut with Reble, Paal Dabba, and 99side, according to Wikipedia. That puts him in a small circle of voices pushing Indian hip-hop across languages.

Why catch the set

Vichaar is part of the festival's homegrown strand, alongside names like Seedhe Maut, Raja Kumari and Dhanda Nyoliwala. If you like your Hindi rap with a designer's eye for visuals and a contest-tested stage presence, this early-career set is worth showing up for.

Tickets

Rolling Loud India takes place December 12-13 in Mumbai, with tickets on the District app. Details at rollingloud.com/india.

item.title: 8 Days in Savannah: 49 Winchester's 'Change of Plans' Is the Castlewood, Virginia Band's Lucille Records / MCA Debut
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: Castlewood, Virginia's 49 Winchester released Change of Plans on Lucille Records / MCA, recorded in eight days with Dave Cobb in Savannah.
item.content:encoded:
The six-piece named for a Castlewood street cut an album executive produced by Dave Cobb, covered Black Sabbath and landed an ACM nomination.

Castlewood, Virginia's 49 Winchester released Change of Plans on May 15, 2026, their debut on Lucille Records / MCA. Dave Cobb executive produced the 10-song album at his Savannah, Georgia studio, where the band recorded it in eight days.

A street name that stuck

The band is named for the Winchester Street address in Castlewood, in Russell County, where frontman Isaac Gibson grew up, Cardinal News reported in 2022. Gibson spotted it on his parents' mailbox when the teenage band still had no name. The outlet said the street sign has been stolen about six times.

Gibson and bassist Chase Chafin are childhood friends who started the group in high school. The first gig was a Heritage Days festival in nearby St. Paul, and the self-titled debut arrived in 2014. For years, members held day jobs; Gibson worked in his family's masonry and building business.

Today's six-piece adds Bus Shelton on lead guitar, Noah Patrick on pedal steel, Tim Hall on keys, and Justin Louthian on drums.

Inside Change of Plans

Saving Country Music called it the band's sixth album and its major-label debut. The headline-grabber is a cover of Black Sabbath's "Changes," which the outlet said began as a tribute to Ozzy Osbourne before taking on a life of its own.

"Oh Savannah," written by Gibson with Jessie Jo Dillon and Chris Tompkins, was inspired by the Savannah sessions. The label also singled out "Slowly" and "Pardon Me" as standout tracks. MCA collaborated with New West Records on the project, and all subsequent releases will be issued exclusively under the MCA banner.

A big year on the road

The band sold out two nights at Nashville's Ryman Auditorium in fall 2025, per the label, and was booked for the Grand Ole Opry on May 12, 2026. They were nominated for Group of the Year at the ACM Awards, and MusicRow named them a 2026 Group/Duo Artist of the Year nominee.

The summer calendar included supporting Eric Church at Red Rocks on July 7, then dates with Tim McGraw, including Virginia Beach on Aug. 6 and Bristow on Aug. 15. A Nov. 13 date in The Woodlands, Texas, with Treaty Oak Revival is also on the books.

"We started this thing from the smallest seed possible," Gibson said in the album announcement, adding that "it finally feels like now is our time to come up."

49 Winchester has 146K Instagram followers as of October 2026.

Where to listen and follow

Signed vinyl of Change of Plans is listed at New West Records. The album is on Lucille Records/MCA.

item.title: Is Tim Barry 'Too Richmond for RVA'? The Richmond, Virginia Avail Frontman Goes Electric on 'Clear Blocks Ahead'
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: Richmond, Virginia's Tim Barry, Avail frontman, released Clear Blocks Ahead on Chunksaah, recorded with the Spacebomb House Band.
item.content:encoded:
The Avail singer cut 13 songs with Spacebomb's house band, with his daughter Lela Jane on four tracks and trains in the song titles.

Richmond, Virginia songwriter Tim Barry released Clear Blocks Ahead on June 12, 2026, through Chunksaah Records. One track title says plenty about where his heart is: "Too Richmond For RVA."

From Avail to acoustic

Barry is the lead singer of Richmond punk band Avail, per Wikipedia. Style Weekly reported in 2010 that he joined the band in 1988 as its drummer before becoming lead singer, and that Avail released six studio albums between 1992 and 2002 and toured Europe ten times.

"Avail never flew a banner about anything except Richmond," Beau Butler told the paper. According to Wikipedia, Barry has performed solo folk music since 2004, with Chunksaah releases including Rivanna Junction, Manchester, 28th & Stonewall, 40 Miler, Lost & Rootless, High on 95, and 2022's Spring Hill.

A full band at Spacebomb

For the new album, Barry weighed nearly 40 songs, some dating to the 1990s, and chose a full-band approach, according to his official store. He cut 13 tracks with the Spacebomb House Band in Richmond, moving away from Spring Hill's Americana toward electric guitars and rock-leaning hooks.

His daughter, Lela Jane Barry, lends her voice to four tracks. A First City Record Store listing says the songs cover the years after the pandemic, including "dad life," train travel, confounding relationships, and the lives of old friends and past acquaintances.

Trains, Roanoke and "Thank You"

Barry's store page describes the songs as full of "margin-dwelling characters," with "a distinct sense of hope." The tracklist leans into the rails and the road, with "Steady Locomotion," "Loads East, Empties West," "Hello From Roanoke" and "Iron City Break[down]."

The album opens with "W.W. Pool" and "Still Lit," runs through "Wreck-less," "Waltzing The Cell," "Miller ; Rhoads," "It Ain't Easy" and "Broken Songs," and closes with "Thank You [For All The Songs]."

Trains have long been part of the story. Style Weekly's 2010 profile noted that Barry keeps detailed journals, leaves graffiti messages on freight trains, and memorializes people he lost in his songs and art.

Discotech listed an Oct. 3 date with Brian Fallon & The Painkillers at San Diego's Casbah. Next comes a hometown show: JamBase lists a Nov. 20, 2026, show at Richmond's The Camel with Julie Karr, Roger Harvey and Sally Rose.

Barry has 29K Instagram followers as of October 2026.

Where to listen and follow

Barry's official store has records and merch at store.timbarryrva.com. Clear Blocks Ahead is out on Chunksaah Records.

item.title: Fea's New Album 'The Nerve' Is About Power and Hypocrisy: Inside the San Antonio, Texas Punk Band's Return
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: San Antonio, Texas punk band Fea released The Nerve on Cosmica Artists, a four-years-in-the-making album taking aim at power and hypocrisy.
item.content:encoded:
The all-woman band born from Girl in a Coma took four years to make its Cosmica Artists debut, with songs in English and Spanish.

San Antonio, Texas punk band Fea is back with The Nerve, a nine-track album that took four years to make. Released May 29, 2026, on Cosmica Artists, the record targets power and hypocrisy, according to the San Antonio Current.

Born from Girl in a Coma

Bassist Jenn Alva and drummer Phanie Diaz founded Fea in 2015 after San Antonio alt-rock band Girl in a Coma broke up, Ghost Cult Magazine reported. The Current notes that Girl in a Coma has since reunited, and that Alva and Diaz spent the past year and a half writing, recording, and touring with the band as well.

The all-woman lineup keeps busy off the stage. Singer Letty Martinez works as a paralegal for an immigration firm, and Diaz owns and operates three San Antonio venues. Guitarist Adrian Conner, who joined in 2022 and also plays in AC/DC tribute act Hell's Belles, makes her Fea album debut here.

What The Nerve is about

Leadoff track "Careful" comes with a video directed by Alva that nods to Bette Midler's "Oh, the Deep" from Beaches, with Martinez in the C.C. Bloom role and her bandmates playing Amelia Earhart, Frida Kahlo and Joan of Arc, per the Current.

"Poison" criticizes Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and health fearmongering, and was inspired partly by Martinez's experience with her son's autism diagnosis. "Paco," the album's second single, deals with a family member's death and the guilt survivors carry. Martinez sings several songs in Spanish.

New label, same punk spine

Fea was first signed to Joan Jett's Blackheart Records, where it released two albums and an EP of covers. The Current reports that Blackheart moved away from developing new artists to focus on Jett, and that its development and promotion approach didn't fit the band's goals for the new record. Ghost Cult notes that Alice Bag produced the second album, No Novelties, and co-produced the self-titled debut with Laura Jane Grace and Lori Barbero.

Cosmica Artists, a Southern California label run by Diaz's old friend Gil Gastelum, leans toward Latin sounds. Melodic Magazine listed June dates in Marfa, Tucson, Mesa, El Paso, Austin, Houston, Dallas, and Little Rock, plus a July 11 show at San Antonio's Rah! Rah! Room.

Melodic also listed September dates with Hell's Belles in Commerce, Texas, and at San Antonio's Sam's Burger Joint. Diaz told the outlet, "San Antonio is such a melting pot of music," and pointed visitors to the Bang Bang Bar.

Fea has 18K Instagram followers as of October 2026.

Where to listen and follow

The Nerve is out now on Cosmica Artists digitally, with vinyl planned later this summer, per the Current. Follow Fea on Instagram for new dates.

item.title: The Shins Turn 30 With Two Unreleased 1996 Songs, and Portland, Oregon's James Mercer Has a Children's Book Coming
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: Portland, Oregon's James Mercer marks 30 years of The Shins with unreleased 1996 songs on a 7-inch and his children's book Book of Dreams.
item.content:encoded:
A 1,000-copy 7-inch revives 'The Living End' and 'All Messed Up,' while Mercer's 'Book of Dreams' lands March 2, 2027.

Portland, Oregon's James Mercer is marking 30 years of The Shins two ways: a limited 7-inch of two previously unreleased 1996 songs, and his first children's book, Book of Dreams, due March 2, 2027. Mercer says the book grew out of talking about dreams with his daughters.

Two songs from 1996

Stereogum reported on July 13, 2026, that the 30th-anniversary 7-inch features "The Living End" and "All Messed Up," two 1996 tracks by Mercer with original drummer Jesse Sandoval. It is limited to 1,000 copies and comes with original art by Mercer from the same period.

Stereogum pointed fans to the band's merch store at kf-merch.com to order. The timing lines up with another milestone: The Shins' debut album, Oh, Inverted World, turned 25 in summer 2026, and the band had been active for about five years before it came out.

Book of Dreams

Random House Studio, an imprint of Random House Children's Books, will publish Book of Dreams, written by Mercer and illustrated by Jacob Escobedo. The 40-page picture book for ages 4 to 8 moves through dreams in rhyming verse, from playful and strange to scary and deep, with dream-journal prompts in the back.

"Dreams were something my daughters and I talked about all the time," Mercer said in the announcement posted by Nasty Little Man. He said he wanted the book "to capture the feeling of moving through those strange nighttime worlds where anything can happen." Editor Maria Correa acquired North American rights. Mercer narrates the audiobook through Listening Library, and an original lullaby from him is on the way.

Escobedo, an Atlanta-based SVP of Creative at Cartoon Network and Adult Swim, has designed album art for The Shins, Broken Bells and DangerDoom. His art for the book is gouache and acrylic, printed with fluorescent pink ink.

From Albuquerque to Portland

Mercer founded The Shins in 1996 in Albuquerque, New Mexico, and later co-founded Broken Bells with Danger Mouse. The two-time Grammy nominee lives in Portland with his family. KOIN called the group a "New Mexico-turned-Portland indie band."

This fall, The Shins and Silversun Pickups were the support acts on Weezer: The Gathering, a 32-date arena run. Consequence listed a Sept. 11 stop at Portland's Moda Center and an Oct. 24 wrap at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles.

The Shins have 135K Instagram followers as of October 2026.

Where to listen and follow

News and tour updates are at theshins.com, and the anniversary 7-inch was offered through kf-merch.com.

item.title: Blackstone, Virginia's Alexander Mack Won a Grammy Before His Debut Album. Now 'You Had To Be There' Is Here
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: Blackstone, Virginia's Alexander Mack, a Grammy winner on Mad Skillz's Words for Days Vol. 1, releases debut LP You Had To Be There.
item.content:encoded:
The Richmond-based keyboardist helped make Mad Skillz's Grammy-winning Words for Days Vol. 1, then dropped a 12-song LP of his own.

Blackstone, Virginia musician Alexander Mack won a Grammy before releasing a full-length album. The Richmond-based singer, songwriter, producer and pianist helped make Mad Skillz's Words for Days Vol. 1, which won Best Spoken Word Poetry Album at the 68th Grammy Awards on Feb. 1, 2026.

By August, he had released his own debut LP, the 12-song You Had To Be There, The Source reported. WTVR CBS 6 called it a deeply personal project that took more than two years to complete.

A first for Nottoway County

Mack, born Matthew Alexander Bagley, is from Blackstone in Nottoway County. The local Courier-Record wrote that his win is "believed to be a first for Nottoway County." Bagley marked the moment on Facebook with three words: "GOD IS GOOD."

He officially moved to Richmond in 2021, according to Richmond Magazine, which credits him as a producer and keyboardist on the Grammy winner. He played keys and handled arranging on the album's tracks from "Wednesday" through "Saturday."

One big jam session

Words for Days Vol. 1 is organized around the days of the week, opening with "Sunday's Service" and closing with "Saturday's Groove." It was recorded at Spacebomb Studio in Richmond's Fan district in April 2025 and credits 14 local collaborators.

"Four or five other musicians and producers and I recorded at Spacebomb, and it was one big jam session," Mack told Richmond Magazine. It was Skillz's first Grammy; his album The Seven Number Ones earned his first nomination in the same category in 2025. Producer Bee Boy$oul accepted the award on his behalf. The album topped nominees including Saul Williams with Carlos Niño & Friends, Queen Sheba, Marc Marcel, and Omari Hardwick with Anthony Hamilton.

What's on You Had To Be There

The Source highlights "Cucumber Cool," "Mango Lady," "Spark" with rising Atlanta-based emcee Will Hill, and "I've Been Waiting" with Mia Broadberry. Trip Carter also appears. The outlet says Mack is inspired by Anderson .Paak.

His stated goal: to leave the world "at least slightly better than I found it."

A hometown stage at the Folk Festival

Mack was booked for the Richmond Folk Festival, the free three-day event on the city's downtown riverfront, Oct. 9–11, 2026. WTVR listed his set for Saturday, Oct. 10, from 3:15 to 4:15 p.m. on the Center for Cultural Vibrancy Stage at Allianz Amphitheater, and he stopped by the station ahead of the weekend. He has also performed at Culture Shock and Richmond's Jazz & Music Festival, per The Source.

Where to listen and follow

You Had To Be There is available on all major streaming platforms, WTVR reported in August.

item.title: Snappy Kaal Rolling Loud India 2026: Meet the Gujarati Rapper Taking Thakkarnagar Global
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: Snappy Kaal, the Gujarati rapper behind "Thakkarnagar Stylee," plays Rolling Loud India on Dec 12 in Mumbai. Here's what to know before his set.
item.content:encoded:
A raw, regional voice from Ahmedabad's streets joins a Mumbai bill topped by Burna Boy and Metro Boomin.

Rolling Loud India just handed one of Gujarat's loudest street voices a festival slot. Snappy Kaal, the rapper who put Thakkarnagar on the hip-hop map, is booked for Saturday, December 12, in Mumbai, alongside Burna Boy, Metro Boomin, and Big Sean.

Who is Snappy Kaal?

Snappy Kaal is a Gujarati rapper from Thakkarnagar. Homegrown profiled him in April 2026 as one of three artists bringing regional language, culture, and class realities into Indian hip-hop, and described his sound as hardcore, raw, and aggressive.

The sound: struggle, slang, Gujarati pride

His lane is unfiltered street storytelling. Themes of struggle, perseverance, and rising above your surroundings run through it, delivered in Gujarati with local slang front and center. That specificity is the point: he represents Gujarati identity rather than sanding it down for a broader audience.

Tracks to know before the set

  • "Thakkarnagar Stylee"
  • "Mun Maara Baapa"
  • "Mathaman"

Homegrown cites these as examples of his street-focused storytelling, social commentary, and blunt self-expression. Queue them up so you can rap along in the crowd.

Why catch him

Festivals like this give regional scenes their moment. Rolling Loud India's lineup, per Rolling Stone India, mixes global names with homegrown acts, and Snappy Kaal is the Gujarati representative on Day One. Expect a raw, high-energy set from an artist whose whole identity is rooted in where he comes from.

Dates and tickets

Rolling Loud India 2026 runs December 12 and 13 in Mumbai. Snappy Kaal plays Saturday, December 12. Tickets are on the District app, with details at rollingloud.com/india. The venue is still to be announced, so watch official channels for updates.

item.title: powli 'Fingertips' Meaning: Berlin's Flirty New Pop Power Move
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: What does powli's 'Fingertips' mean? We break down the Berlin singer-songwriter's flirty hip-hop-meets-pop single and the story behind her rise.
item.content:encoded:
Musicboard Berlin backed her with a grant. 'Fingertips' shows why. Here's what the song is really saying.

Berlin has no shortage of rising pop talent, but powli has something many emerging artists would love to have: an official vote of confidence from the city itself. If her single "Fingertips" has you curious, here's what the song is about and who's behind it.

Who Is powli?

powli is a Berlin-based singer-songwriter, multi-instrumentalist and producer. According to Musicboard Berlin, the city's music funding body, she plays piano and guitar and blends pop with rock, indie and hip-hop. Musicboard lists Billie Eilish and Lana Del Rey among her main influences.

In 2023, Musicboard Berlin awarded powli a €6,000 grant as part of its Project Scholarship program, linked to her work on a debut album titled cinnamon. Her Spotify bio calls that funding a crucial boost for her career. Her first single was "Money."

What Is "Fingertips" About?

"Fingertips" was released on January 19, 2024, and her bio says it marks the beginning of a new musical identity that blends hip-hop and pop.

Lyrically, the song plays with power and flirtation. The narrator opens with questions about where things are headed between two people, then flips the script. She knows she's someone's favorite, she gets her way without hesitating, and she doesn't feel like explaining herself. The key twist: since the other person claimed not to care, she decides she gets to be unfair, too. It's a playful turnaround, taking someone's indifference and using it as permission to have fun on her own terms.

That theme matches how her bio describes her writing: confident, empowering lyrics alongside more personal themes drawn from her own life, dreams and the people around her.

Why "Fingertips" Works

A lot of flirty pop songs are about chasing someone. "Fingertips" is about holding the cards. That shift in perspective is what makes it stick. It's cheeky without being cold, and it fits neatly beside the Billie Eilish and Lana Del Rey influences Musicboard highlights, artists who also love playing with power and mood.

The song is also performing. At the time of writing, "Fingertips" has more than 14,000 plays on Spotify, a solid number for an independent artist still building her audience.

What's Next for powli?

item.description: Portland, Oregon's Ruban Nielson of Unknown Mortal Orchestra and Jared Mattson released FEAR on Jagjaguwar, recorded in Palm Springs.
item.content:encoded:
The UMO leader and The Mattson 2's Jared Mattson met online as fans, then cut a whole album in Palm Springs in a couple of days.

Portland, Oregon's Ruban Nielson, the mind behind Unknown Mortal Orchestra, took a detour in 2026. FEAR, his collaborative album with Jared Mattson of The Mattson 2, arrived June 5 on Jagjaguwar, and it was imagined for lonely, in-between places like motels, abandoned gas stations, and parking lots.

Fans first, collaborators second

Stereogum reported that Nielsen and Mattson connected online in 2024 as fans of each other's music. That June, they recorded the album over a couple of days in Palm Springs, California.

A product listing from New Zealand retailer JB Hi-Fi says they recorded and mixed everything in Palm Springs, with Matt Colton mastering at Metropolis Studios in London. In Mattson's account, "FEAR" was finished two days later, and Nielsen told him, "Let's make more that sound exactly like this."

Music for motels and empty parking lots

Mattson told Stereogum he imagined music set in transitional, impersonal spaces, music that "could sit inside that loneliness without trying to fix it." He summed up the mood as "calm without anesthesia."

The seven-track album runs "HIGH T," "RIVER RAFTING," "TESTAROSSA," "AMERICAN EAGLE," "WEDGIE," "TOUCHDOWN" and "RAZOR BLADE." Lead single "AMERICAN EAGLE" arrived with a video directed by Mark Francis.

Mattson brings his own history of cross-band projects. Stereogum's archive shows The Mattson 2 releasing music with Chaz Bundick in 2016 and 2017, and appearing on Toro y Moi's 2020 Joe Bataan cover "Ordinary Guy."

From Auckland to Portland

Unknown Mortal Orchestra began in 2009 as Nielson's solo project in Auckland, New Zealand, and is now based in Portland, according to Wikipedia. Before that, he formed the band The Mint Chicks in Auckland, and he moved to the United States in 2007.

Fat Possum released UMO's 2011 debut. Jagjaguwar has released the band's albums since 2013, a run that includes II, Multi-Love, Sex & Food and the 2023 double album V. Wikipedia lists "Multi-Love," "Hunnybee," "Can't Keep Checking My Phone" and "So Good at Being in Trouble" among the project's notable songs.

Nielson stayed busy before FEAR, too. In 2025, UMO issued the instrumental album IC-02 Bogotá, the Curse EP, and the singles "Earth 1" and "Boys With The Characteristics Of Wolves."

As of October 2026, Unknown Mortal Orchestra has 156K Instagram followers.

Where to listen and follow

Stream and buy UMO's catalog on the official Unknown Mortal Orchestra Bandcamp. FEAR is out on Jagjaguwar.

item.title: Zippy Raises $20 Million to Modernize the Most Overlooked Corner of the American Housing Market
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: Zippy raises a $20M Series C from Saluda Grade to expand manufactured housing loans beyond 27 states and launch new products for communities and retailers.
item.content:encoded:
The manufactured-home lender's Series C from Saluda Grade follows more than $600 million in capital commitments secured this year.

Manufactured homes are one of the last truly affordable paths to owning a home in America. Financing them, however, has long been slow, paper-heavy and underserved by mainstream lenders. Zippy has just raised $20 million to change that.

The tech-enabled lender and loan servicer closed a Series C round with Saluda Grade as the sole investor, committing through its growth equity strategy, FinTech Global reported. Beyond capital, Saluda Grade will support Zippy on credit, capital markets, balance sheet management and product development.

A Lender Built for One Kind of Home

Founded in 2021, Zippy focuses exclusively on manufactured housing finance. It works with manufactured housing communities, retailers, dealers and wholesale partners, and has built its own loan origination platform covering digital applications, partner tools, underwriting, standardized paperwork and data infrastructure.

"Manufactured housing is already one of the most compelling affordable homeownership solutions in America, but it needs a financing system that is just as modern and efficient as the homes themselves," co-founder and CEO Ben Halliday said.

The Numbers Behind the Round

Zippy currently operates in 27 states. In 2026 alone, it has secured more than $600 million in capital commitments, the lending capacity that lets it fund loans at scale. The new equity gives the company room to keep growing that balance sheet while investing in technology.

"Zippy has built an impressive platform in one of the most overlooked sectors of housing finance," said John Stepp, head of ventures at Saluda Grade.

Why Manufactured Housing Is Having a Moment

With home prices and mortgage rates squeezing first-time buyers, manufactured homes offer a far lower entry price than site-built houses. Yet buyers often face higher rates and fewer lending options, in part because many manufactured homes are financed as personal property rather than traditional real estate. Lenders that can underwrite these loans efficiently stand to capture a market that big banks have largely ignored.

That gap is the opportunity Zippy is targeting: a vertical, software-driven lender that understands the economics of manufactured home communities and dealers better than generalist mortgage shops.

Saluda Grade's involvement is also strategic. The firm is known for its work in residential credit and capital markets, expertise that matters for a lender whose growth depends on reliably funding and selling loans. A sole-investor round from a specialist backer suggests conviction in Zippy's underwriting, not just its software.

For buyers, the promise is simple: faster approvals, clearer paperwork and fewer dead ends at the dealership or community office. For the industry, a well-capitalized digital lender could add competition to a segment where options have historically been thin.

What Comes Next

Zippy says the funding will help it expand beyond its current 27-state footprint, launch new loan products through community, retail and wholesale channels, and build out its technology and balance sheet capacity.

If it succeeds, Zippy could help make one of America's most affordable housing options easier to finance, and turn a long-neglected corner of lending into a serious fintech category.

item.title: Affinity Labs Raises $2 Million to Turn Influencers Into Software Founders With AI
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: London's Affinity Labs raises $2M pre-seed led by Fuel Ventures to co-found AI-powered software brands with creators, plus a £497K Innovate UK grant.
item.content:encoded:
The London startup co-founds apps with creators like Olivia Bowen, and says its portfolio revenue has been doubling month over month.

Creators have mastered attention. What most of them have not built is a business that runs without them on camera. London startup Affinity Labs wants to fix that by co-founding software companies with creators, and it just raised $2 million to scale the idea.

The pre-seed round was led by Fuel Ventures, with Antler co-investing, Tech.eu reported. Angel investors from Google DeepMind, Meta and Playfair VC joined, along with creator Marcello Ascani and Kyra CEO Devran Amaratunga Karaca. Affinity Labs also secured a £497,787 grant from Innovate UK, part of UK Research and Innovation.

Creators as Co-Founders

The model is simple to explain and hard to execute. Every product Affinity Labs launches is co-founded with a creator who brings an existing, engaged audience. Affinity Labs supplies the technology, product and operations needed to turn that audience into a paying software brand.

"Creators are the most underleveraged founders in the world," CEO Edoardo Ricci said. "Affinity Labs exists to be that infrastructure, we co-found every product with a leading creator."

Ricci runs the company alongside COO Ahmed Eltom and CTO Sunny Panchal.

AI Does the Heavy Lifting

What makes the approach scalable is a proprietary AI-powered development system that automates stages of the product lifecycle, from identifying software ideas and matching them with creator partners to building, operating and growing the products. That automation is what lets a small team run a portfolio rather than a single app.

Early Traction

Affinity Labs has launched four creator-led brands so far. Interior Design Clinic, built with Olivia Bowen, reached No. 34 in the App Store's Lifestyle category. Archives, built with Basel Ghazoghli, has more than 75,000 users and ranks among the top 200 Education apps. According to the company, portfolio revenue has averaged 100% month-over-month growth over the past three months, meaning it has roughly doubled each month.

Why It Matters

The creator economy has largely monetized through brand deals, merch and consumer products like beverages and cosmetics. Software is a different animal: higher margins, recurring revenue and products that can grow even when the creator takes a break. If AI lowers the cost of building apps far enough, a creator's audience may become the most valuable distribution channel a new software company can have.

What's Next

Affinity Labs will use the funding to expand its portfolio, support existing products and grow its product, growth and engineering teams. Part of the capital, including the Innovate UK grant, will go toward its AI product development technology.

The company plans to launch its first products with U.S. creators in late 2026 and has set an ambitious target of more than 200 creator-led software brands by 2030. For American influencers wondering what comes after the sponsorship era, that could make Affinity Labs a name worth knowing.

item.title: Elevation Capital Bets $10.5 Million That an AI-Powered Indian Studio Can Build Your Next Phone Game Obsession
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: Spill Games raises $10.5M Series A led by Elevation Capital to scale its AI-led mobile game studio, Compass engine and casual puzzle titles worldwide.
item.content:encoded:
Bengaluru's Spill Games, maker of Cozy Finds and Zen Math Crossword, lands a Series A roughly six months after its seed round.

The next puzzle game eating up your commute may be coming out of Bengaluru, and it may have been tested, tuned and scaled with help from AI. Spill Games, a two-year-old mobile studio, has raised $10.5 million (about ₹100 crore) in a Series A round led by Elevation Capital.

Existing investors Centre Court Capital and PeerCapital also joined the round, Inc42 reported. The raise comes roughly six months after Spill closed a $3.1 million seed round in April, a fast follow-on that signals strong early traction.

An AI-Led, Portfolio-Driven Studio

Founded in 2024 by Om Misra, Tapan Ranjan and Harsh Garg, Spill builds free-to-play casual, puzzle and hybrid-casual titles for a global audience. Its portfolio includes Cozy Finds, Sticker by Number, Zen Math Crossword, Bird Rescue Jam and Grill Master, monetized through advertising and in-app purchases.

"We started Spill because we love making and playing games," Misra told DealStreetAsia. The business model, however, is built on discipline rather than passion alone. Spill launches games quickly to test assumptions, then uses player feedback and in-game data to decide which titles deserve more investment and which get cut.

The Compass Engine

At the center of that process is Compass, Spill's in-house engine that brings together tools for analytics, player retention, monetization and live operations. Because the infrastructure is reused across games, the studio says it can shorten development and testing cycles, targeting speeds roughly four times faster than traditional approaches.

That speed matters in casual mobile gaming, where hits are unpredictable and user acquisition costs can sink a studio that bets too heavily on any single title.

Built in India, Played in America

Spill is part of a new wave of Indian studios building for players overseas. At the time of its seed round, the company said about half of its users came from the United States, followed by Brazil and Japan. It previously set goals of testing more than 20 prototypes within 18 months and launching five to ten profitable titles.

The timing is notable. India's government has banned real-money gaming, pushing investor attention toward studios that earn money from ads and in-app purchases instead of wagers. Spill sits squarely in that safer lane.

Where the Money Goes

Spill plans to use the new capital to scale its existing games, expand its development pipeline, strengthen the AI and technology capabilities of Compass, acquire users and selectively grow its team.

For Elevation Capital, one of India's most active early-stage firms, the bet is that a data-driven studio can turn hit-making from luck into a repeatable system. If Spill pulls that off, the American players already making up half its audience will be the ones who notice first.

item.title: 5 Things to Know Before You Buy Rapid Rewards Points
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: Before you buy Southwest Rapid Rewards points, learn five facts on pricing, real value, Companion Pass rules, limits, and cancellations.
item.content:encoded:
Southwest's points work differently from every other airline's. Five facts decide whether buying them helps you.

Disclosure: YourInfoDaily may earn a commission if you buy through links in this article. Offers change and are often targeted, so confirm the terms in your own account before buying.

Before you buy Rapid Rewards points, know these five things: your discount is personal, a point is worth about 1.3 cents, bought points don't count toward the Companion Pass, the purchase isn't airfare to your card, and point bookings are unusually easy to cancel. Together, they tell you when buying helps and when it doesn't.

1. Your discount is not the same as everyone else's

Southwest's standard price is 3 cents per point. It discounts points regularly, but not equally. One Mile at a Time reported that during a sale running September 2 to October 2, 2026, different members were offered 35%, 45%, or 50% off. Award Travel Finder's tracker, updated October 9, 2026, listed a 50% discount through October 29.

On a purchase of 60,000 points, those tiers look like this:

  • 50% off: $900, or 1.5 cents per point.
  • 45% off: $990, or 1.65 cents per point.
  • 35% off: $1,170, or 1.95 cents per point.

The discount in that sale applied only to purchases of at least 3,000 points in one transaction.

What to do: log in and look at your own offer before you read anyone's verdict on the sale, including this one. A 50% offer and a 35% offer lead to different answers.

2. A point is worth about 1.3 cents, almost every time

With most airlines, a point's value swings widely, and experts hunt for sweet spots. Southwest is different. Frequent Miler explains that award prices depend on demand and the flight's cash price, rising and falling with the fare. Any seat for sale can be booked with points.

The result is predictable value. Frequent Miler's benchmark is 1.3 cents per point. One Mile at a Time estimates 1.1 to 1.5 cents.

That predictability works against buyers. No hidden jackpot makes points bought at 1.5 cents suddenly worth 4 cents. One Mile at a Time concludes that buying at 1.5 cents or more rarely makes sense, because points usually redeem for less.

What to do: treat buying as a way to complete a booking, not as a discount on travel.

3. Bought points do not count toward the Companion Pass

The Companion Pass lets a named companion fly with you for only the taxes. Frequent Miler requires 135,000 qualifying points in a calendar year.

Purchased points do not qualify. Neither do points transferred from another member, most bonus points, or points transferred in from hotel partners or Chase Ultimate Rewards. What does count: base points from paid flights, Southwest credit card spending, card welcome bonuses, and many partner activities.

What to do: if the pass is your target, put your money into paid flights and card spending. Buy points only for redemptions.

See the Rapid Rewards offer on your account.

4. There are limits, and your card sees a different merchant

According to One Mile at a Time, you can buy up to 60,000 points per day, with no annual limit. That is unusually open. Most programs cap purchases annually.

The sale is processed by Points.com, not by Southwest. Your credit card will not record it as an airline purchase, so do not expect an airfare bonus category to apply. One Mile at a Time suggests using a card with a minimum spending requirement or one with strong everyday rewards.

What to do: choose a card for its base earning rate, and buy only what your booking needs. The lack of an annual cap isn't a reason to stock up.

5. Points bookings are easy to undo, and points never expire

This is the best argument for holding Rapid Rewards points at all.

  • Cancellations. Frequent Miler notes that you can cancel award flights for no fee up to 10 minutes before departure, with points returned immediately. One Mile at a Time adds that a canceled cash ticket becomes a travel credit for a future flight, while redeposited points can be used for anyone.
  • Changes. If your flight price drops after you book, Frequent Miler says changing to a cheaper fare returns the difference in points.
  • Expiration. Rapid Rewards points do not expire, and no activity is needed to keep them. Closing your account forfeits them.

What to do: if your travel dates are uncertain, a points booking gives you a clean exit. After you book, check the price again periodically. If it falls, rebook and collect the difference.

Top up your Rapid Rewards balance.

So when should you buy?

  • Buy when you are a few thousand points short of a flight you are ready to book. A 3,000-point top-up at 50% off costs about $45.
  • Consider buying when your plans may change, and you value getting points back more than holding a travel credit.
  • Do not buy to pay for a whole trip at a 35% or 45% discount, to chase the Companion Pass, or because a sale is ending. Another sale will follow.

A quick self-check

  • What discount does my account show?
  • What is the cash fare, and what is the points price?
  • How many points am I actually missing?
  • If I cancel, would I rather hold points or a travel credit?

Two more notes. Southwest offers a Cash + Points option, which Frequent Miler says yields poor value per point. And free checked bags now depend on your fare, elite status, or a Southwest credit card, so include bag costs when you compare a Southwest fare with a competitor's.

FAQ

How much are Rapid Rewards points worth?

About 1.3 cents each by Frequent Miler's benchmark, with a typical range of 1.1 to 1.5 cents.

Is there a limit on how many Southwest points you can buy?

Up to 60,000 per day, with no annual cap.

Do Rapid Rewards points expire?

No.

Can I get a refund on points I buy?

Treat purchases as final and read the terms shown at checkout before you pay.

item.title: Vinci Pharmaceuticals Closes $8M Series A for Needle-Free Retinal Drug Implant
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: Vinci Pharmaceuticals closed an $8M+ Series A led by Dynagrow Capital to advance EPIPLANT, a sustained-release episcleral implant for retinal disease, toward a 2027 trial.
item.content:encoded:
The New Jersey eye care company is preparing its EPIPLANT implant for a first-in-human trial in 2027 as an alternative to repeated eye injections.

Vinci Pharmaceuticals, a specialty eye care company based in Avon-by-the-Sea, New Jersey, has closed a Series A financing of more than $8 million to advance its EPIPLANT drug delivery platform. Dynagrow Capital led the round, with support from MintPharma Capital.

The raise follows $8.5 million in seed financing, bringing Vinci's total funding to more than $16.5 million.

What EPIPLANT Is

Many of the most common treatments for retinal diseases, including those affecting the macula, are delivered by injection directly into the eye, often every month or two. The treatment burden is heavy, and many patients stop treatment early, which can lead to vision loss.

EPIPLANT is designed to avoid that. It is a bioerodible implant placed on the outer surface of the eye, against the sclera, that releases medication to the retinal tissues over time without injections into the eye. The platform can currently deliver small-molecule drugs and is designed to work with a range of active ingredients.

The technology was developed in the lab of retina specialist Karl Csaky, MD, PhD, and is licensed from the Retina Foundation of the Southwest in Dallas. Vinci says it holds multiple granted patents and has completed preliminary preclinical testing.

How the Money Will Be Used

The proceeds will fund manufacturing, testing and release of its lead product, EPIPLANT VCI-002, under good manufacturing practice standards, as well as a planned Phase 1/2a first-in-human clinical trial in 2027.

Co-founder, chairman and CEO Philip A. Gioia described the financing as an important step toward that first human study. Dynagrow Capital managing director Sarah Hassan said a needle-free option could help reduce the high dropout rates caused by the burden of current treatment.

Why It Matters

Retinal diseases such as age-related macular degeneration and diabetic macular edema are among the leading causes of vision loss, and the drugs used to treat them form one of the largest markets in ophthalmology. Much of the industry's recent innovation has focused on making treatments last longer between injections.

Vinci is aiming further, removing the intraocular injection entirely. The approach still has to show in humans that it can deliver enough drug to the retina safely and consistently. With the Series A closed, the company has funding to manufacture clinical supply and bring EPIPLANT to its first patients.

item.title: What Is Atlas Atomics? Ramaswamy's $1.9B Nuclear Bet
item.dc:creator: YourInfoDaily
item.description: Atlas Atomics is the stealth nuclear startup co-founded by Vivek Ramaswamy. It raised about $400M at a $1.9B valuation to build a heavy water reactor.
item.content:encoded:
The stealth company raised about $400M in a General Catalyst-led Series A to build a heavy water reactor that does not need enriched uranium.

Atlas Atomics, a stealth nuclear energy startup co-founded and backed by Vivek Ramaswamy, has raised about $400 million in a Series A round at a valuation of roughly $1.9 billion, Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

General Catalyst is leading the round, with Andreessen Horowitz participating. Atlas Atomics, General Catalyst and a16z declined to comment, so the terms have not been confirmed by the company.

Who Is Behind Atlas Atomics

Ramaswamy, the entrepreneur and Ohio gubernatorial candidate, is a co-founder and backer. Day-to-day leadership sits with co-founder Kevin Gan, who spent more than 15 years investing in energy companies, most recently at hedge fund Millennium and before that at D.E. Shaw & Co.

The company's chief nuclear officer is Balendra Sutharshan, a former chief operating officer of Oak Ridge National Laboratory, the Department of Energy's largest science and energy lab and a central institution in American nuclear research. VentureTerminal lists the company in Columbus, Ohio.

The Technology

Atlas Atomics is developing an improved heavy water reactor. Unlike most reactors operating in the US, heavy water designs can run on natural uranium rather than enriched uranium. That matters because enrichment is expensive and global capacity is concentrated in a handful of suppliers, with Russia historically among the largest.

Avoiding enrichment could make Atlas's reactors cheaper to fuel and less exposed to supply bottlenecks. In a letter to Utah's Governor's Office of Energy Development, Gan said the technology aims to provide reliable power, expand production of medical and industrial isotopes and support nuclear fuel recycling.

Why It Matters

A $400 million Series A is one of the largest early-stage rounds in nuclear energy, and it arrives as demand for round-the-clock, carbon-free power climbs, driven largely by AI data centers. Tech companies have signed deals to restart old reactors and back new designs, and investors have followed with large checks into advanced nuclear startups.

Heavy water reactors are not new. Canada's CANDU fleet has run on the approach for decades. That track record could help with regulators, though any new design still faces a long licensing process with the Nuclear Regulatory Commission. For Ohio, the company's ties to the state add to a growing presence in energy and advanced manufacturing investment.

Valuing a stealth company at nearly $2 billion before it has publicly shown a reactor is a large bet on its team. With a former Oak Ridge executive running the nuclear program and two of venture capital's biggest firms behind it, Atlas Atomics has the money and credibility to make its case.
